explanation: Independent demonstratives take an acute by convention, even when spoken sentence prominence falls elsewhere. Demonstrative that's likewise remains accented.
Explicitly contrastive demonstrative determiners take an acute. Do not infer this contrast from ordinary sentence-initial capitalization or prior mention alone.
Independent possessive his is accented, unlike the weak determiner in his book. Copular is stays weak by default.
A personal pronoun used as an independent answer takes its strong accented form. Sentence-final position alone does not require an accent, as in neutral I saw him.
The noun can uses its full accented pronunciation, not the weak modal form. Apply the same role-first distinction to lexical will, might, must, and the month or name May.
